added_lemmas.statement: For an instance \(I=(M,a,X,Y,c,L,B)\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\), let \(C_X\) and \(C_Y\) be the weak components of \(X\) and \(Y\) in the underlying undirected full graph. If \(C_X\ne C_Y\), then \(X=a_X\) is not a Beckers actual cause of \(Y=a_Y\). If \(C_X=C_Y=C\), restriction to \(C\) preserves existence of a Beckers witness and its exact minimum deletion cost. More precisely, every global witness restricts to a witness on \(C\) of no larger cost, and every witness on \(C\) extends, with the same cost, by retaining all edges and using the actual assignment on every other weak component.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(H\in\mathcal H(G)\) and let \(w\) be an alternate solution witnessing that \(X=a_X\) causes \(Y=a_Y\). By \(\texttt{lem:canonical-replay}\), for every endogenous vertex \(Z\),
\[
 Q_Z^{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)}(a_{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)})=\{a_Z\}. \tag{1}
\]
If a nonintervened endogenous vertex \(Z\) satisfies \(w_Z\ne a_Z\), then some retained parent \(p\in\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)\) satisfies \(w_p\ne a_p\). Indeed, if every retained parent were actual, the structural membership of \(w_Z\) would place it in the left side of (1), which is the singleton \(\{a_Z\}\). Repeating this predecessor step terminates because \(G\) is acyclic. It cannot terminate at an exogenous root, because the context fixes every exogenous value at its actual value, and it cannot terminate at a nonintervened endogenous root, because (1) applies to its empty retained-parent row. Hence it terminates at the sole intervened vertex \(X\). Applied to \(w_Y\ne a_Y\), this gives a retained directed path from \(X\) to \(Y\). Since \(H\subseteq G\), the vertices \(X\) and \(Y\) must lie in the same weak component of \(G\). This proves the negative assertion when \(C_X\ne C_Y\).

Now suppose \(C_X=C_Y=C\). No edge of \(G\) has exactly one endpoint in \(C\). Consequently every parent of a vertex of \(C\) lies in \(C\), and restricting the domains and local tables to the vertices of \(C\) gives an explicit acyclic instance \(I|_C\) with the same query and the same costs on \(E(G[C])\).

First restrict a global witness \((H,w)\) to \(C\). If a deleted edge of \(G[C]\) had a retained alternative path in \(H[C]\), the same path would violate \(H\in\mathcal H(G)\); hence \(H[C]\in\mathcal H(G[C])\). All local actual-row equalities and all alternate memberships at vertices of \(C\) are unchanged, because these vertices have no parents outside \(C\). Thus \(\texttt{lem:canonical-replay}\) makes \((H[C],w|_C)\) a witness for \(I|_C\). Its cost is
\[
 \sum_{e\in E(G[C])\setminus E(H[C])}c(e)
 \le
 \sum_{e\in E(G)\setminus E(H)}c(e), \tag{2}
\]
where the inequality uses \(c(e)\ge0\) from \(\texttt{ass:nonnegative-rational-cost}\).

Conversely, let \((H_C,w_C)\) witness the restricted instance. Define
\[
 H'=H_C\cup\bigcup_{D\ne C}G[D],
 \qquad
 w'_q=
 \begin{cases}
 (w_C)_q,&q\in C,\\
 a_q,&q\notin C,
 \end{cases} \tag{3}
\]
where \(D\) ranges over the other weak components. Every deleted edge of \(H'\) lies in \(C\), and any path between its endpoints also lies in \(C\); legality of \(H_C\) therefore proves \(H'\in\mathcal H(G)\). At a vertex outside \(C\), all parents are retained and actual, so its projected actualized relation at both the actual and alternate input is
\[
 A_Z(a_{\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z)})=\{a_Z\}. \tag{4}
\]
At vertices in \(C\), the local checks are exactly those of the restricted witness. Hence canonical replay proves that (3) is a global witness. No edge outside \(C\) is deleted, so its cost equals that of \((H_C,w_C)\).

Taking minima in the two directions gives
\[
 \min_{\text{global witnesses}}\sum_{e\notin H}c(e)
 =
 \min_{\text{witnesses on }C}\sum_{e\in E(G[C])\setminus E(H_C)}c(e), \tag{5}
\]
with both empty minima equal to \(+\infty\). Equation (3) is the claimed cost-nonincreasing normalization outside the relevant component.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(I=(M,a,X,Y,c,L,B)\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\) have connected underlying undirected full graph of cycle rank one, with unique simple cycle \(K\). There is at most one directed edge \(e^\star\in E(K)\) whose complementary arc \(K\setminus\{e^\star\}\) is a directed path from the tail of \(e^\star\) to its head. Every Beckers witness has a cost-nonincreasing normalization consisting of an alternate assignment \(w\in R(U\cup V)\), one support row \(\rho_Z\in R(\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z))\) for each \(Z\in V\setminus\{X\}\), the row-difference deletion set
\[
 D^0(w,\rho)=\{p\to Z:Z\ne X,\ \rho_{Z,p}\ne w_p\},
\]
and, only when deleting \(e^\star\) would leave its complementary arc retained, one additional cycle edge. Conversely, every such normalized tuple satisfying the local actual-row hitting tests and \(w_Z\in A_Z(\rho_Z)\) for \(Z\ne X\) is a Beckers witness. Its exact minimum cost is the minimum of at most \(2|E(K)|-1\) explicit min-sum programs on a factor graph of cycle rank one. The recurrences in the proof evaluate them using \(O(L^7)\) arithmetic and indexed-address operations, every finite rational encountered has \(O(B+\log(L+1))\) bits, and the computation returns either a positive witness with an exact optimum certificate or polynomial-size infeasibility tables forming a separating cut.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(D_H=E(G)\setminus E(H)\). By \(\texttt{lem:canonical-replay}\), a feasible causal witness is equivalently a graph \(H\in\mathcal H(G)\), the equalities
\[
 Q_Z^{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)}(a_{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)})=\{a_Z\}
 \qquad(Z\in V), \tag{6}
\]
and an assignment \(w\in R(U\cup V)\) satisfying
\[
 w_U=a_U,\qquad w_X\ne a_X,\qquad w_Y\ne a_Y,
 \qquad
 w_Z\in Q_Z^{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)}(w_{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)})
 \quad(Z\in V\setminus\{X\}). \tag{7}
\]
The equation at \(X\) is absent from (7) because the alternate model intervenes on \(X\). Since the candidate event is a singleton and \(X\ne Y\), its minimality clause has no nonempty proper subevent. Thus (6)--(7), together with graphical legality, characterize the causal query; they do not define it.

Let \(e=p\to Z\) be deleted. If its underlying edge is not on \(K\), a second undirected path between \(p\) and \(Z\) would create another undirected cycle. If \(e\in E(K)\), its only possible alternative undirected path is \(K\setminus\{e\}\). Hence
\[
 p\leadsto_H Z
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 K\setminus\{e\}\text{ is directed from \(p\) to \(Z\) and all its edges are retained}. \tag{8}
\]
Give each edge of \(K\) a sign according as it agrees or disagrees with a fixed cyclic order. An edge has the orientation property in (8) exactly when its sign is opposite to every other sign. Two distinct edges cannot both have this property, because a simple cycle has a third edge, whose sign would then have to be opposite to both opposite signs. Thus there is at most one exceptional edge \(e^\star\). If it is absent, every subgraph is legal. If it exists, (8) and the definition of \(\mathcal H(G)\) give
\[
 H\in\mathcal H(G)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 e^\star\notin D_H
 \ \text{or}\ 
 D_H\cap\bigl(E(K)\setminus\{e^\star\}\bigr)\ne\varnothing. \tag{9}
\]
These are precisely the exceptional-edge and complementary-arc bits carried by \(\operatorname{UnicycleHandle}\).

Fix a witness \((H,w)\). For every \(Z\ne X\), (7) and the definition of projection supply \(\rho_Z\in R(\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z))\) such that
\[
 w_Z\in A_Z(\rho_Z),
 \qquad
 \rho_Z|_{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)}=w|_{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)}. \tag{10}
\]
Set
\[
 D^0=\{p\to Z\in E(G):Z\ne X,\ \rho_{Z,p}\ne w_p\}. \tag{11}
\]
Equation (10) implies \(D^0\subseteq D_H\). If \(D^0\) satisfies (9), put \(D=D^0\). Otherwise (9) implies
\[
 e^\star\in D^0,
 \qquad
 D^0\cap(E(K)\setminus\{e^\star\})=\varnothing. \tag{12}
\]
Because \(D_H\) is legal and contains \(D^0\), there is an edge
\[
 f\in D_H\cap(E(K)\setminus\{e^\star\}). \tag{13}
\]
Put \(D=D^0\cup\{f\}\). In either case \(D\subseteq D_H\), and (9) proves \(G\setminus D\in\mathcal H(G)\).

Let
\[
 S_Z(D)=\{p\in\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z):p\to Z\notin D\}.
\]
Since \(D\subseteq D_H\), the set \(S_Z(D)\) contains \(\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)\). Equation (6) and \(\texttt{lem:local-hitting-equivalence}\) say that \(\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)\) hits every member of \(\mathcal B_Z\), so its superset does also. Applying the same lemma again yields
\[
 Q_Z^{S_Z(D)}(a_{S_Z(D)})=\{a_Z\}
 \qquad(Z\in V). \tag{14}
\]
For \(Z\ne X\), every parent retained under \(D\) agrees between \(\rho_Z\) and \(w\), by (11); the optional edge \(f\) only removes a matching constraint. Consequently
\[
 w_Z\in A_Z(\rho_Z)
 \subseteq Q_Z^{S_Z(D)}(w_{S_Z(D)}). \tag{15}
\]
Equations (9), (14), and (15), followed by canonical replay, prove that \((G\setminus D,w)\) is a witness. Since \(D\subseteq D_H\) and all costs are nonnegative,
\[
 \sum_{e\in D}c(e)\le\sum_{e\in D_H}c(e). \tag{16}
\]

Conversely, suppose \(w\), rows \(\rho_Z\), and a set \(D\) have this normalized form, satisfy (9), obey \(w_U=a_U\), \(w_X\ne a_X\), \(w_Y\ne a_Y\), and satisfy
\[
 w_Z\in A_Z(\rho_Z)\quad(Z\ne X),
 \qquad
 S_Z(D)\cap\Delta\ne\varnothing
 \quad(Z\in V,\ \Delta\in\mathcal B_Z). \tag{17}
\]
The hitting equivalence gives (14), while the row-difference construction gives (15). Graphical legality follows from (9), so canonical replay makes this tuple a Beckers witness. This proves both directions of the normalized-certificate characterization. Finiteness of every domain makes each finite optimum attainable.

We now expose the finite programs. For a support row, put
\[
 \delta^0_{p\to Z}(\rho,w)=\mathbf 1\{\rho_{Z,p}\ne w_p\}\quad(Z\ne X),
 \qquad
 \delta^0_{p\to X}=0. \tag{18}
\]
If \(e^\star\) is absent, use one unconstrained mode. If it exists, use the following \(2|E(K)|-1\) modes:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{mode \(0\):}&\delta^0_{e^\star}=0;\\
\text{mode \(g\), \(g\in E(K)\setminus\{e^\star\}\):}
 &\delta^0_{e^\star}=\delta^0_g=1;\\
\text{repair mode \(\bar f\), \(f\in E(K)\setminus\{e^\star\}\):}
 &\delta^0_{e^\star}=1,\quad
 \delta^0_h=0\ \text{for all \(h\in E(K)\setminus\{e^\star\}\),
 and \(f\) is additionally deleted.}
\end{array} \tag{19}
\]
Mode \(0\) and the modes \(g\) cover every legal base set \(D^0\); the repair modes cover exactly (12)--(13). Duplication of a base set in several modes does not change a minimum.

For mode \(b\), let \(f_b=f\) in repair mode \(\bar f\) and let \(f_b=\bot\) otherwise. For values of \(Z\) and all its parents, define
\[
 \Phi_Z^b(w_Z,w_{\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z)})
 =
 \min_{\tau}
 \left\{
   \sum_{p:p\to Z\in D_Z^b(\tau,w)}c(p\to Z)
 \right\}, \tag{20}
\]
where \(\tau=\rho_Z\in R(\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z))\) and \(w_Z\in A_Z(\rho_Z)\) if \(Z\ne X\), whereas \(\tau=\star\) is the only choice at \(Z=X\), and
\[
 D_Z^b(\tau,w)
 =
 \{p\to Z:Z\ne X,\ \rho_{Z,p}\ne w_p\}
 \cup
 \{f_b:f_b=p\to Z\text{ for some \(p\)}\}. \tag{21}
\]
The minimum is subject to the mode constraints in (19) for edges entering \(Z\) and to
\[
 \bigl(\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z)\setminus
 \{p:p\to Z\in D_Z^b(\tau,w)\}\bigr)\cap\Delta\ne\varnothing
 \qquad(\Delta\in\mathcal B_Z), \tag{22}
\]
and is \(+\infty\) if no row satisfies them. Each mode restriction is unary in an edge indicator and is therefore assigned exactly to the factor at that edge's head.

For every \(q\in U\cup V\), define
\[
 \psi_q(v)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&q\in U\text{ and }v=a_q,\\
 0,&q=X\text{ and }v\ne a_X,\\
 0,&q=Y\text{ and }v\ne a_Y,\\
 0,&q\in V\setminus\{X,Y\},\\
 +\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases} \tag{23}
\]
Let \(C^\star(I)\) be the minimum deletion cost among Beckers witnesses, with the empty minimum equal to \(+\infty\). The normalization (10)--(16) maps every causal witness to a feasible program point of no larger cost, and (17) maps every finite program point to a causal witness of exactly its displayed cost. Hence the causal target and the explicit input functional are related by the proved equality
\[
 C^\star(I)
 =
 \min_b\ \min_{w\in R(U\cup V)}
 \left\{
  \sum_{Z\in V}\Phi_Z^b(w_Z,w_{\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z)})
  +\sum_{q\in U\cup V}\psi_q(w_q)
 \right\}. \tag{24}
\]

To solve (24), form a bipartite factor graph with a variable vertex for each \(q\in U\cup V\), a factor vertex for each \(Z\in V\), and edges from factor \(Z\) to its child variable \(Z\) and all parent variables. Contracting every factor--child edge recovers the underlying undirected graph of \(G\); each contraction preserves cycle rank. Thus the factor graph has cycle rank one. Choose a variable \(q_0\) on its unique cycle, condition on \(q_0=v\), substitute \(v\) into every incident factor, and remove \(q_0\). The remainder is a forest. On every rooted component use
\[
 m_{q\to Z}(x_q)
 =
 \psi_q(x_q)+\sum_{T\in N(q)\setminus\{Z\}}m_{T\to q}(x_q), \tag{25}
\]
and
\[
 m_{Z\to q}(x_q)
 =
 \min_{x_{N(Z)\setminus\{q\}}}
 \left\{
  \Phi_Z^b(x_{N(Z)})
  +\sum_{r\in N(Z)\setminus\{q\}}m_{r\to Z}(x_r)
 \right\}. \tag{26}
\]
An induction from the leaves proves that each message is the minimum sum of potentials on the sending side conditional on its boundary value. The leaf case is (25) or (26) with an empty sum. Removing the receiving edge separates the remaining sending-side branches, so adding their conditional minima and then minimizing the newly internal boundary values proves the induction step. Summing component minima, adding \(\psi_{q_0}(v)\), minimizing over \(v\in R(q_0)\), and then minimizing over (19) therefore evaluates exactly (24).

All potentials are explicitly computable. There are at most \(L\) modes and factors; a deliberately coarse bound gives at most \(L^2\) output-and-parent assignments per factor, at most \(L\) candidate support rows per assignment, and at most \(L^2\) indexed bad-row coordinate incidences to scan for (22). Hence constructing the potentials and evaluating (25)--(26) takes \(O(L^7)\) arithmetic and indexed-address operations. Every finite program value is a sum of a subset of the input edge costs. Scaling by the product of their positive denominators uses at most \(B+1\) denominator bits, and summing at most \(L\) scaled numerators adds at most \(\lceil\log_2(L+1)\rceil\) bits. Thus every finite value has \(O(B+\log(L+1))\) bits and exact comparison has polynomial bit complexity.

A finite optimum records its mode, conditioned value, minimizing choices in (25)--(26), assignment \(w\), support rows, and optional repair edge. Equations (9), (17), and the supplied rows verify the witness, and rescanning all message minima verifies optimality. If every mode is infinite, the finite entries of the same message arrays are closed under every feasible local extension but omit every accepting conditioned-root state; they therefore form a polynomial-size separating cut whose closure is verified by the same recurrences.

For the smallest legality stress test, take binary vertices \(U\to X\to Y\) and \(U\to Y\), actual value zero, \(X=U\), and \(Y=X\wedge U\). Here \(e^\star=U\to Y\). Producing \(w_X=w_Y=1\) forces support row \((U,X)=(1,1)\) at \(Y\), so \(D^0=\{U\to Y\}\), which violates (9). Repair by deleting \(U\to X\) makes the projected actual row of \(X=U\) contain one; repair by deleting \(X\to Y\) makes the parent-free projected actual row of \(Y\) contain the output one from row \((1,1)\). Both repairs violate (14), and every mode is rejected exactly as full-graph legality requires.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(I=(M,a,X,Y,c,L,B)\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\), let \(C_X\) and \(C_Y\) be the weak components of \(X\) and \(Y\) in the underlying undirected full graph. If \(C_X\ne C_Y\), then \(X=a_X\) is not a Beckers actual cause of \(Y=a_Y\), the minimum witness cost is \(+\infty\), and \(C_X\) is a separating cut. Suppose instead that \(C_X=C_Y=C\) and that the connected graph \(G[C]\) has cycle rank at most one; no restriction is imposed on any other weak component. Every witness cost-nonincreasingly normalizes by retaining every edge and using the actual assignment outside \(C\), so existence and exact minimum cost equal those for the restricted instance \(I|_C\). If the rank is zero, the minimum is the value-path functional
\[
 \min_{s_i\in R(P_i)\setminus\{a_{P_i}\}}
 \sum_{i=1}^{m}C_i(s_{i-1},s_i),
\]
and the linear-arithmetic compiler and verifier apply. If the rank is one, the exceptional-edge modes and factor-graph recurrences specified by \(\operatorname{UnicycleHandle}\) compute the exact minimum. Uniformly over both ranks, an algorithm uses \(O(L^7)\) arithmetic and indexed-address operations and polynomial bit time, every finite rational encountered has \(O(B+\log(L+1))\) bits, and it returns either a positive witness with an exact optimum certificate or a polynomial-size separating cut.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Apply \(\texttt{lem:component-restriction-normalization}\). If \(C_X\ne C_Y\), that lemma proves noncausation. Moreover, no edge leaves the weak component \(C_X\), so \(C_X\) contains \(X\), excludes \(Y\), and is closed under every directed edge; it is a directly checkable separating cut. The causal minimum is therefore \(+\infty\).

Suppose \(C_X=C_Y=C\). The same lemma proves the equality
\[
 C^\star(I)=C^\star(I|_C) \tag{27}
\]
between the global causal minimum and the minimum on the relevant-component restriction, and it gives the asserted cost-nonincreasing normalization. Constructing \(C\) and \(I|_C\) takes a single scan of the explicit graph and tables; its encoding sizes \(L_C\) and \(B_C\) satisfy \(L_C\le L\) and \(B_C\le B\).

If \(G[C]\) has cycle rank zero, it is a tree because \(C\) is connected. Thus \(I|_C\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{forest}}\). By \(\texttt{thm:value-path-optimum}\), a witness exists exactly when the displayed value-path minimum is finite, and that minimum is \(C^\star(I|_C)\). The algorithms and three certificate types of \(\texttt{thm:compiler-verifier-equivalence}\) compute and verify this value using \(O(L_C)\) arithmetic and indexed-address operations with \(O(B_C+\log(L_C+1))\)-bit intermediates. Extending its positive certificate by the actual assignment and all edges outside \(C\), as in the component lemma, preserves the cost and truth of the decoded global claim. A negative path or reachability cut inside \(C\) remains separating in \(G\), because no edge joins distinct weak components.

If \(G[C]\) has cycle rank one, the restricted graph is connected and unicyclic, so \(\texttt{lem:connected-unicycle-min-sum}\) applies. It proves that the exceptional-edge min-sum functional equals \(C^\star(I|_C)\), computes it in \(O(L_C^7)\) operations with \(O(B_C+\log(L_C+1))\)-bit finite values, and supplies the stated positive, optimum, or separating certificate. Again the component lemma extends any positive certificate without cost and makes a component-level separating table a global one.

Combining each branch with (27), \(L_C\le L\), and \(B_C\le B\) proves all semantic, optimum, certificate, arithmetic, and bit-complexity assertions. Components outside \(C\) were never restricted; they are eliminated only by the proved normalization, not by redefining the causal target.

added_lemmas.statement:
The class \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{chain}}\) is contained in the broader Beckers class
\[
 \{I\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}:\text{the underlying undirected graph of \(G[V]\) is a tree}\}.
\]
Consequently, deciding whether \(X=a_X\) is a Beckers actual cause of \(Y=a_Y\) is NP-complete on this broader endogenous-causal-tree graph shape, and its zero-cost, zero-budget restriction is NP-hard. This transfer concerns Beckers actualized structural simplification and full-graph deletion legality; it does not identify Beckers causation with Halpern--Pearl causation or modify the published Halpern--Pearl causal-tree theorem.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{ass:endogenous-chain}\), every instance of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{chain}}\) has \(G[V]\) equal to one directed chain from \(X\) to \(Y\). Forgetting orientations gives a path, hence a tree. This proves the displayed class inclusion. The reduction in \(\texttt{thm:chain-np-completeness}\) is therefore already a reduction into the broader endogenous-tree graph-shape class, and it uses zero edge costs and budget zero. NP-hardness transfers upward by set inclusion.

It remains to prove membership for the broader class rather than assume it from the restricted theorem. For any explicit instance, guess a retained graph \(H\subseteq G\), a complete alternate assignment \(w\), and one original supporting row for every nonintervened projected-table membership. Reachability searches in \(H\) check, for each deleted \(p\to Z\), that \(p\not\leadsto_H Z\). A scan of the explicitly stored rows checks
\[
 Q_Z^{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)}(a_{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)})=\{a_Z\}
 \qquad(Z\in V),
\]
and the supplied rows check every alternate projected membership. The verifier also checks fixed exogenous values, \(w_X\ne a_X\), \(w_Y\ne a_Y\), and, when a budget is present, the exact rational deletion-cost sum. Each operation is polynomial in the explicit input length and rational bit length. By \(\texttt{lem:canonical-replay}\), acceptance is equivalent to a legal full-setting Beckers simplification and alternate solution; singleton minimality is automatic. Thus the problem is in NP on all of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\), and in particular on the displayed endogenous-tree subclass. Together with transferred NP-hardness this proves NP-completeness. The proof uses only the common graph shape when comparing with the published causal-tree setting; its semantic equivalence is nowhere assumed.

proposed_core_edits.name: UnicycleHandle

proposed.name: UnicycleHandle
proposed.def: Identify the weak full-graph component shared by \(X\) and \(Y\); dispatch cycle rank zero to the value-path compiler and cycle rank one to the exceptional-edge, two-arc min-sum program, while retaining every other component at actuality.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The handle is no longer an open-problem placeholder: the connected unicycle program is complete, and component normalization localizes it to the query-relevant weak component.

proposed.name: Relevant-component forest/unicycle handle
proposed.construction: Given an explicit instance, first isolate the weak full-graph component containing \(X\) and \(Y\). Distinct components give a reachability cut. On a common component of cycle rank zero, \(\operatorname{UnicycleHandle}\) dispatches to the value-path compiler. On a common component of cycle rank one, it cuts the unique factor-graph cycle at a boundary variable and carries the exceptional-edge reachability mode---shortcut retained, complementary arc already broken, or one specified repair edge---jointly with the local nonactual-value state; all other weak components are retained at their actual assignments.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The prior construction incorrectly described the unicycle case as unresolved and did not include the proved weak-component reduction.

The connected-full-graph theorem is subsumed by the stronger proved theorem requiring cycle rank at most one only in the weak component containing the query; migrating inbound edges promotes the actual frontier without mislabeling a widening as a narrowing.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\bigl(\mathbf 1\{X=a_X\text{ is a Beckers cause of }Y=a_Y\},C^\star(I)\bigr)\), where \(C^\star(I)=\min\bigl(\{\sum_{e\in E(G)\setminus E(H)}c(e):(H,w)\text{ is a canonical Beckers witness}\}\cup\{+\infty\}\bigr)\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The old estimand used the forest-only path symbol \(\operatorname{OPT}\) as though it already named the causal minimum on the cycle-rank-one branch; this replacement keeps the same causal object while separating it from the identifying program.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: On instances covered by \(\texttt{thm:relevant-component-polynomial-frontier}\), let \(C_X,C_Y\) be the weak components of \(X,Y\), and for their common component put \(r(C)=|E(G[C])|-|C|+1\). Then \(C^\star(I)=+\infty\) if \(C_X\ne C_Y\); if \(r(C)=0\), \(C^\star(I)=\min_{s_i\in R(P_i)\setminus\{a_{P_i}\}}\sum_{i=1}^{m}C_i(s_{i-1},s_i)\); and if \(r(C)=1\), \(C^\star(I)=\min_b\min_{w\in R(C)}\{\sum_{Z\in V\cap C}\Phi_Z^b(w_Z,w_{\operatorname{Pa}_{G[C]}(Z)})+\sum_{q\in C}\psi_q(w_q)\}\), with \(b,\Phi^b,\psi\) the explicit exceptional-edge modes and local potentials in \(\texttt{lem:connected-unicycle-min-sum}\). In all cases the causal indicator equals \(\mathbf 1\{C^\star(I)<+\infty\}\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The forest path formula alone is stale after promoting the exact frontier to relevant components of cycle rank one; the piecewise functional records the disconnected, tree, and unicycle maps proved by the replacement theorem.

prose_updates.tldr: Beckers defines actual causation by counterfactual dependence in an actualized structural simplification, but does not provide an exact algorithmic frontier. For finite explicit local tables, tractability localizes to the weak component of the full graph on \(U\cup V\) containing the query: different components give an immediate negative cut; cycle rank zero gives the exact linear-arithmetic value-path compiler; and cycle rank one gives an exact exceptional-edge min-sum algorithm with positive, optimum, and separating certificates, while all other components may be arbitrary. A shared-selector reduction proves NP-completeness even for deterministic binary models whose endogenous graph is one directed chain, so hardness transfers to the broader Beckers class having the published endogenous causal-tree graph shape. This transfers only graph shape and does not conflate Beckers with Halpern--Pearl semantics.

project_justification.niche: The novel computational scope uses finite explicitly encoded tables and restricts only the weak full-graph component shared by \(X\) and \(Y\) to cycle rank at most one. Component separation leaves every other weak component unrestricted. The condition is on the full graph over \(U\cup V\), not on the endogenous graph \(G[V]\) used by the published Halpern--Pearl causal-tree result.
project_justification.fill: The project proves an extensional forest compiler, an exact relevant-component frontier through cycle rank one, explicit additive min-sum functionals, and independently checkable positive, optimality, and negative certificates. The selector-and-clause reduction proves Beckers NP-completeness on a deterministic binary endogenous chain and therefore on the broader endogenous-tree graph-shape class, while the shared-selector obstruction explains why endogenous-only propagation cannot audit full-graph deletion legality.

prose_updates.related_work: Beckers2025Actual, Section 5.1, Definitions 13, 15, and 16 on pages 523--524 and Section 6, Definitions 18 and 19 and Proposition 20 on page 525, supplies the structural-simplification and actual-causation semantics; the proof of Proposition 20 appears on page 532. It is semantic prior art and contains no compiler, exact cost functional, or tractability frontier. Beckers2025NCM supplies set-valued equations and topological counterfactual semantics, while finite explicit encoding is a new computational-scope restriction here. The earlier UAI version of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable, Section 4.1 and Theorems 4.2--4.3, propagates families of endogenous path-value sets for Halpern--Pearl causes on causal trees. The positive result here instead restricts the query-relevant weak component of the full graph on \(U\cup V\) to cycle rank at most one and explicitly audits actualized projection and deleted-edge reachability. The hardness reduction has a directed-chain endogenous graph, so its graph shape lies inside the published endogenous causal-tree shape and transfers NP-hardness upward for Beckers semantics; it does not transfer or alter the Halpern--Pearl theorem. EiterLukasiewicz2002Complexity and AleksandrowiczEtAl2014 show that complexity is definition-sensitive, but neither treats Beckers deletion. IbrahimRehwaldPretschner2019SAT and IbrahimPretschner2020Optimization concern Boolean Halpern--Pearl encodings, and ReydDiaconescuDessalles2025Search gives approximate Halpern--Pearl-style search rather than exact Beckers certificates. No semantic equivalence between these causal definitions is claimed.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact positive frontier proved here stops when the weak full-graph component containing \(X\) and \(Y\) has cycle rank at least two. No claim is made for general full-graph treewidth FPT, succinct mechanisms, continuous domains, negative deletion costs, unrestricted polynomial negative certificates, or unrestricted parsimonious certificate counting. The selector reduction gives a bijection only for normalized certificates; unrestricted successful retained graphs may encode one satisfying assignment in several ways and normalization need not preserve a counting interpretation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved result assumes finite nonempty domains, total explicitly listed set-valued tables, an acyclic full graph, a supplied actual solution, and nonnegative rational deletion costs. It localizes the full-graph restriction: only the weak component containing both query variables must have cycle rank at most one, and distinct query components are certified negative; other components may be arbitrary. This is not the published Eiter--Lukasiewicz endogenous causal-tree class, because shared exogenous roots participate in Beckers reachability legality. The deterministic binary endogenous-chain reduction nevertheless lies inside that published graph shape, so NP-hardness transfers upward only as a Beckers graph-class statement. Cycle rank at least two in the relevant full component, general treewidth parameterization, and unrestricted certificate counting remain outside the claims.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem identifies the largest proved positive class in this note by the query-relevant full component, preserves the exact optimum, and supplies auditable positive, optimality, and negative certificates even when irrelevant components have arbitrary cycle structure.
statement_notes.gap: Published Halpern--Pearl causal-tree propagation constrains the endogenous graph and does not establish the Beckers exceptional-edge reachability modes, actual-row hitting tests, or weak-component normalization used here.
statement_notes.consumer: An explicit-support backend for the \(\texttt{actualcauses}\) Python package can dispatch disconnected, forest, and unicycle relevant components and verify the returned witness, optimum, or separating cut.

statement_notes.justification: The corollary prevents an unsound endogenous-tree fast path: the chain reduction is already a subclass of that graph shape, while its shared exogenous selectors retain the Beckers hardness mechanism.
statement_notes.gap: The transfer is a graph-class inclusion for Beckers semantics, not a reduction between Beckers and Halpern--Pearl definitions; prior Halpern--Pearl complexity results therefore do not themselves prove this corollary.
statement_notes.consumer: The backend may use the relevant full component as its tractability test and must not infer tractability from the endogenous causal-tree shape alone.

proofs.proof_tex:
We first prove membership in \(\mathrm{NP}\), using only the explicit-input hypotheses and hence, in fact, for every singleton query in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\).  A certificate consists of a retained edge set \(E(H)\subseteq E(G)\), an alternate assignment \(w\in R(U\cup V)\), and, for each \(Z\in V\setminus\{X\}\), an index for a full parent row \(\rho_Z\in R(\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z))\).  The verifier checks
\[
 w_U=a_U,\qquad w_X\ne a_X,\qquad w_Y\ne a_Y,                                      \tag{1}
\]
and checks that \(\rho_Z\) agrees with \(w\) on every retained parent of \(Z\) and that
\[
 w_Z\in A_Z(\rho_Z)\qquad (Z\in V\setminus\{X\}).                                  \tag{2}
\]
Thus the row \(\rho_Z\) witnesses the required membership of \(w_Z\) in the projected table at the alternate retained-parent assignment.  The verifier also checks, for every \(Z\in V\),
\[
 Q_Z^{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)}(a_{\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)})=\{a_Z\}.                  \tag{3}
\]
To check (3), it scans every explicitly listed row \(r\) whose retained coordinates equal their actual values, replaces the one full actual row by \(\{a_Z\}\), and rejects exactly when an allowed nonactual output occurs.  Finally, for every deleted edge \(p\to Z\), a graph search checks that there is no nonempty retained directed path from \(p\) to \(Z\).  By \(\mathrm{def:legal\mbox{-}retained\mbox{-}graph}\), this last test is equivalent to \(H\in\mathcal H(G)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:canonical\mbox{-}replay}\), (2)--(3) and graphical legality are equivalent to a legal full-setting Beckers structural simplification in which the intervention \(X\leftarrow w_X\) has the complete alternate solution \(w\).  Conditions (1) therefore make the certificate accepting exactly when it witnesses the singleton causal query.  Actuality holds by the supplied actual solution, and minimality is automatic because the singleton candidate has no nonempty proper subcandidate.

Every guessed object is a list of indices into the explicit input.  The scans above take polynomially many operations in \(L\), and reachability can be checked once for each of at most \(L\) deleted edges.  For a budgeted instance the verifier additionally sums the costs of the deleted edges and compares the sum with the budget.  There are at most \(L\) summands, and elementary integer numerator--denominator arithmetic has bit length polynomial in \(B+L\).  Hence both the unbudgeted and budgeted problems are in \(\mathrm{NP}\).

For hardness, reduce from the problem in \(\mathrm{lem:three\mbox{-}sat\mbox{-}np\mbox{-}complete}\).  Delete repeated occurrences of a literal within a clause and discard every tautological clause.  These operations preserve satisfiability and leave at most three distinct literals in each remaining clause.  If an empty clause occurs, map to the construction below applied to the fixed unsatisfiable formula \((z)\wedge(\neg z)\); if no clause remains, map to the construction applied to the fixed satisfiable formula \((z)\).  We may therefore assume henceforth that the input \(\varphi=\bigwedge_{j=1}^m K_j\) has \(m\ge1\), variables \(z_1,\ldots,z_n\), and between one and three distinct, noncomplementary literals in every clause.

For every \(z_i\), create two binary exogenous roots \(T_i\) and \(F_i\).  Create binary endogenous variables in the chain
\[
 X\longrightarrow S_1\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow S_n
 \longrightarrow C_1\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow C_m=Y.                  \tag{4}
\]
All actual values are zero, and the structural table of \(X\) is constantly zero.  If \(p\) denotes the chain predecessor of \(S_i\), add the two root edges \(T_i\to S_i\) and \(F_i\to S_i\), and define the deterministic table
\[
 S_i(p,T_i,F_i)=
 \begin{cases}
 T_i\wedge F_i,&p=0,\\
 T_i\mathbin\oplus F_i,&p=1.
 \end{cases}                                                                       \tag{5}
\]
For a positive occurrence of \(z_i\) use the root \(T_i\), and for a negative occurrence use the root \(F_i\).  If the resulting distinct literal roots of \(K_j\) are \(\ell_{j1},\ldots,\ell_{jk_j}\), add their edges to \(C_j\) and set
\[
 C_j(p,\ell_{j1},\ldots,\ell_{jk_j})
 =p\wedge\bigl(\ell_{j1}\vee\cdots\vee\ell_{jk_j}\bigr).                       \tag{6}
\]
Equations (5)--(6) are total deterministic binary tables.  The all-zero assignment is a solution: (5) gives zero when all its arguments are zero, and (6) gives zero when \(p=0\).  The full graph is acyclic because every root edge enters a later vertex of (4), and its endogenous induced graph is exactly (4).  A selector has total indegree three and a clause has total indegree \(1+k_j\le4\).  Every displayed parent is genuine: in (5), fixing \((T_i,F_i)=(1,0)\) makes the output vary with \(p\), while fixing \(p=1\) and the other root at zero makes the output vary with either root; in (6), fixing one literal root at one makes the output vary with \(p\), and fixing \(p=1\) and all other literal roots at zero makes the output vary with the selected literal root.  Each table has at most \(2^4=16\) rows, and there are at most three literal incidences per clause, so the graph and all tables are constructed in time polynomial in \(|\varphi|\).  The constructed instance therefore belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{chain}}\).

We next establish the invariant forced by any accepting witness.  Let \(H\) and \(w\) be such a witness.  Since the domains and actual values are binary, (1) gives \(w_X=w_Y=1\), while every exogenous root remains at zero.  If a nonintervened endogenous variable \(Z\) has \(w_Z=1\), then at least one retained parent of \(Z\) has value one.  Indeed, if every retained parent had its actual value zero, alternate membership would put \(w_Z\) in the left side of (3), which is \(\{0\}\), a contradiction.  Starting at \(Y\) and iterating this implication backwards, the value-one parent cannot be exogenous.  Each vertex of (4) other than \(X\) has exactly one endogenous parent, so that parent and its incident chain edge must respectively have value one and be retained.  Induction back to \(X\) proves
\[
 w_{S_i}=w_{C_j}=1\quad\text{for all \(i,j\)},
 \qquad E((4))\subseteq E(H).                                                       \tag{7}
\]

Consider the two root edges entering \(S_i\).  If both were retained, their alternate values would be \((T_i,F_i)=(0,0)\); together with the retained predecessor value one from (7), equation (5) would force \(w_{S_i}=0\), contradicting (7).  If both were deleted, then in the actual retained-parent row the predecessor is zero and the deleted coordinates may be completed by \((T_i,F_i)=(1,1)\).  This is not the full actual row, so actualization leaves (5) unchanged there, and (5) outputs one.  Consequently the projection in (3) would contain one, again a contradiction.  Hence exactly one of
\[
 T_i\to S_i,qquad F_i\to S_i                                                       \tag{8}
\]
is deleted.  Call its tail the selected root.  Define a Boolean assignment \(\alpha\) by
\[
 \alpha(z_i)=\mathrm{true}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T_i\to S_i\text{ is deleted}. \tag{9}
\]
Equivalently, \(T_i\) is selected when \(z_i\) is true and \(F_i\) is selected when \(z_i\) is false.

Suppose first that \(\varphi\) has a satisfying assignment \(\alpha\).  Select roots according to (9), delete every outgoing edge of every selected root, and retain every other edge; call the resulting graph \(H_\alpha\).  Each deleted edge has a selected root as its tail, and that root has no retained outgoing edge.  Thus no deleted edge has a retained directed bypass, and \(H_\alpha\in\mathcal H(G)\) by \(\mathrm{def:legal\mbox{-}retained\mbox{-}graph}\).  At a selector, precisely one root coordinate is deleted and the other is retained at zero.  With the retained predecessor at its actual value zero, (5) is then zero for both completions of the deleted coordinate.  Hence (3) holds at every selector.  At a clause, the retained chain predecessor has actual value zero, so (6) is zero for every completion of all deleted literal coordinates; (3) holds there as well.  No edge enters \(X\), so its actualized empty-parent row is \(\{0\}\).  Therefore (3) holds at every endogenous vertex.

Intervene with \(X\leftarrow1\), fix all exogenous roots at zero, and assign value one to every vertex after \(X\) on (4).  At \(S_i\), choose the full support row having predecessor one, selected root coordinate one, and unselected root coordinate zero.  Equation (5) outputs one, and this row agrees with every retained parent.  Since \(\alpha\) satisfies \(K_j\), some literal of \(K_j\) has its selected root as parent.  Its incoming edge to \(C_j\) was deleted; set that coordinate to one, set every retained root coordinate to its exogenous value zero, and use predecessor one.  Equation (6) then outputs one.  These rows verify (2).  Thus \(\mathrm{lem:canonical\mbox{-}replay}\) yields a Beckers witness changing \(Y\) from zero to one, so \(X=0\) is a cause of \(Y=0\).

Conversely, suppose the constructed instance has a Beckers witness.  Recover \(\alpha\) from (8)--(9).  Fix a clause \(C_j\).  By (7), its retained chain predecessor has value one and \(w_{C_j}=1\).  A supporting row for its projected-table membership must therefore make at least one literal-root coordinate equal to one, by (6).  Let \(r\) be such a root.  Since the alternate exogenous value of \(r\) is zero, the edge \(r\to C_j\) must be deleted; otherwise a support row agreeing with retained-parent values would have that coordinate zero.  If \(r\) were unselected, its edge \(r\to S_i\) would be retained by (8), where \(i\) is the variable represented by \(r\).  Equation (7) retains the entire chain segment from \(S_i\) through \(S_n,C_1,\ldots,C_j\).  Hence
\[
 r\to S_i\to S_{i+1}\to\cdots\to S_n\to C_1\to\cdots\to C_j                    \tag{10}
\]
would be a retained directed path from the tail to the head of the deleted edge \(r\to C_j\), contradicting \(H\in\mathcal H(G)\).  Therefore \(r\) is selected.  If \(r=T_i\), the corresponding positive literal is true under (9); if \(r=F_i\), the corresponding negative literal is true.  Thus every clause contains a true literal, and \(\alpha\) satisfies \(\varphi\).

We have constructed a polynomial many-one reduction satisfying
\[
 \varphi\text{ is satisfiable}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 X=0\text{ is a Beckers actual cause of }Y=0.                                      \tag{11}
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{lem:three\mbox{-}sat\mbox{-}np\mbox{-}complete}\), (11) proves \(\mathrm{NP}\)-hardness, and the verifier above proves \(\mathrm{NP}\)-completeness.  Setting \(c(e)=0\) for every edge and setting the budget to zero satisfies the nonnegative rational cost restriction and makes the budget constraint equivalent to mere witness existence, so the same reduction proves the stated budgeted hardness.

As the smallest boundary check, the one-clause formula \((z)\) selects \(T\), deletes \(T\to S\) and \(T\to C\), and has the all-one endogenous alternate solution.  For \((z)\wedge(\neg z)\), (8) selects exactly one of \(T,F\); making the clause for the other literal equal to one would delete that unselected root's clause edge while retaining its path through \(S\), violating (10).  Thus the construction accepts the former and rejects the latter, in agreement with (11).  The proof concerns decision certificates only and makes no claim that unrestricted witnesses are counted parsimoniously.

added_lemmas.statement: On the broader class of instances \(I\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\) for which the endogenous induced graph \(G[V]\) is a directed causal tree containing a directed path from \(X\) to \(Y\), deciding whether the singleton event \(X=a_X\) is a Beckers actual cause of the singleton event \(Y=a_Y\) is \(\mathrm{NP}\)-complete.  In particular, \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{chain}}\) is a subclass of this endogenous causal-tree graph shape, the graph restriction studied by Eiter and Lukasiewicz~\cite{EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable}.  This is a transfer of graph-shape complexity for Beckers structural-simplification semantics; it does not identify that causal predicate with any Halpern--Pearl predicate studied on the same graph shape.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def:chain\mbox{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:endogenous\mbox{-}chain}\), every instance in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{chain}}\) has \(G[V]\) equal to one directed chain from \(X\) to \(Y\).  The underlying undirected graph of a chain is a tree, and its displayed orientation supplies a directed path from \(X\) to \(Y\).  Hence
\[
 \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{chain}}
 \subseteq
 \{I\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}:G[V]\text{ is a directed causal tree containing a directed \(X\)-to-\(Y\) path}\}. \tag{12}
\]
The restriction theorem \(\mathrm{thm:chain\mbox{-}np\mbox{-}completeness}\) and (12) imply \(\mathrm{NP}\)-hardness on the class on the right: the identical instances and the identical Beckers yes/no predicate are used, so no semantic translation is involved.

For membership, use the retained-graph, alternate-assignment, and support-row certificate from the first part of the proof of \(\mathrm{thm:chain\mbox{-}np\mbox{-}completeness}\).  That verification uses only explicit finite tables, the actual-row tests, the reachability test in \(\mathrm{def:legal\mbox{-}retained\mbox{-}graph}\), and the equivalence in \(\mathrm{lem:canonical\mbox{-}replay}\); it does not use determinism, binarity, bounded indegree, or the chain restriction.  All of those inputs and tests are available for every member of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\), so the broader causal-tree restriction is in \(\mathrm{NP}\).  Combining membership with the transferred hardness proves \(\mathrm{NP}\)-completeness.  The reference to the endogenous causal-tree shape is therefore purely graph-theoretic, while the verified witness relation remains Beckers structural simplification throughout.
